profile.reading:
Intergate Seattle East Building 3 stands at 3333 South 120th Place in Tukwila, King County, Washington, part of the Tukwila site Sabey Data Centers markets today as a single campus called SDC Seattle, a few miles south of downtown Seattle and about three miles from Sea-Tac International Airport. Building 3 is one of the buildings in the cluster along South 120th Place that public mapping data still labels Intergate.East, alongside Building 1 nearby and Building 2 next door at 3311 South 120th Place, distinct from the separate Intergate.West cluster of buildings Sabey also owns a few blocks away on Tukwila International Boulevard.

Sabey Data Centers is the data center subsidiary of Sabey Corporation, a Puget Sound commercial real estate and construction company founded in 1972 by Dave Sabey that built its early business as a major industrial and office landlord in the Seattle area through the aerospace driven growth of the 1970s and 1980s. Sabey's own company history describes its move into data centers as tracing back to a tenant vacating one of its buildings during the dot com collapse of the early 2000s, leaving Sabey with an empty large scale technical shell, now counted as SDC Seattle Building 5, that the company recognized as an opportunity in a market starting to demand purpose built computing space. Sabey formalized that pivot in 2010 by partnering with institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors to create Sabey Data Centers as a dedicated operating company, which today describes its national portfolio as more than four million square feet of mission critical space across six campuses in Washington, New York, Texas, and Virginia, with more in development.

On power and scale, Sabey's own site describes SDC Seattle as a whole running on hydroelectric power delivered by Seattle City Light, with more than 90 MVA of aggregate utility power delivered to the campus through redundant feeds, backup generators rated at 2.5 MW apiece with 72 hour runtime at peak load, about 9,500 tons of installed HVAC capacity, and over a million square feet of total space. These figures describe the entire Tukwila site, covering both the Intergate.East cluster where Building 3 sits and the separate Intergate.West cluster, not any single building within it, and Sabey does not publish a building level IT load, utility power, or generator count specific to Building 3. Sabey's certifications for the SDC Seattle campus as a whole include HIPAA and HITECH alignment, PCI DSS, SSAE 18 SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2, LEED Gold, and ISO 27001, again applied at the campus level rather than to individual buildings.

No King County Assessor parcel record, City of Tukwila building permit, or construction and occupancy date specific to Building 3 was identified in this pass, and no trade press coverage naming this building individually, as opposed to the SDC Seattle campus as a whole, was found either. The building's position between Building 2 and the rest of the South 120th Place cluster is consistent with the three East side buildings having been developed and numbered together, but no document establishing the exact order or dates of that development was found in public sourcing during this pass.
profile.capacity_note: not published at the building level. Campus wide total is 54 MW (operator figure) across the Tukwila campus, not applied to this individual building.
profile.research_note: WebSearch was exhausted this session (200 of 200) before this facility group, so research relied on direct WebFetch of Sabey Data Centers' own site (locations page, about page, homepage) plus this database's stored osm_tags, which supplied the confirmed 3333 South 120th Place address for this building and 3311 South 120th Place for neighboring Building 2. Sabey's current marketing treats the whole Tukwila property as one campus, SDC Seattle, and does not break out East vs West sub campus figures or per building specs, so the campus_power_note here reuses the same figures already on file for sibling Building 2 (osm:way/205724881) for consistency across the campus. No King County Assessor or City of Tukwila permit data was accessible in this pass.

profile.campus_power_note: SDC Seattle / Intergate East campus wide figures, not assigned to any single building including this one. Per Data Center Dynamics, 2025: 54 MW total capacity across roughly 1.2 million square feet, six buildings, plus 6 MW of additional Tier III critical power the operator said was scheduled online by December 1, 2025. Per Sabey Data Centers' own site: more than 90 MVA of aggregate utility power delivered through redundant feeds, backup generators rated 2.5 MW apiece with 72 hour runtime at peak load, and about 9,500 tons of installed HVAC capacity across the campus.

reading.body:
Intergate Seattle East Building 3 sits at 3333 South 120th Place in Tukwila, Washington, part of the SDC Seattle campus that Sabey Data Centers operates as a single property across six buildings totaling more than 1.2 million square feet. Building 3 is one of three structures in the Intergate.East cluster, but Sabey publishes no power or capacity figures at the building level, only for the entire campus. The operator's own site describes the whole SDC Seattle campus running on hydroelectric power from Seattle City Light, backed by more than 90 MVA of utility power delivered through redundant feeds and generators rated 2.5 MW each with 72 hour runtime.

The Tukwila campus as a whole holds 54 MW of published IT capacity across all six buildings, ranking third by published capacity in Washington state and representing ninety percent of the state's published data center megawatts. That 54 MW spreads across 1.2 million square feet and roughly 9,500 tons of installed cooling, which at typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack would imply roughly 1,350 racks across the entire campus, though that estimate depends entirely on the actual tenant mix and workload type. Sabey does not publish which portion of this capacity lies in Building 3 or any of its sister buildings.

The campus holds certifications for HIPAA, HITECH, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, LEED Gold, and ISO 27001, which qualify it to host healthcare and financial services workloads under specific compliance regimes. Sabey built this portfolio by converting an early 2000s industrial shell into purpose-built data center space, a pivot the company formalized in 2010 through a partnership with National Real Estate Advisors. Building 3's own construction date and specific power allocation within the campus remain unpublished, making it impossible to measure this particular structure's contribution to the state's AI infrastructure from the operator's disclosed specifications alone.
